rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING TERRORISM, PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Anti-Terrorism Act of 2004.\" This bill defines and punishes the act of terrorism. It states that terrorism is committed by any person or group of persons, who, with the intent of creating a common danger, terror, panic, or chaos to the public, commits any of the following: 1) murder, homicide, serious physical injuries, less serious physical injuries, kidnapping and serious illegal detention, grave threats, and grave coercions; 2) arson; 3) threatening to inflict substantial damage or actually inflicting damage to infrastructures or property used as a public utility; 4) manufacture, possession, acquisition, transport, supply, use or sale of explosives, biological agent, chemical agent, nuclear weapon, materials or equipment and instruments; 5) attacking or threatening to attack, or committing any other unlawful acts against networks, servers, computers, and other information and communications systems; and 6) willful destruction of natural resources.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04839

rows.title_short: Covergence Policy Act of the Philippines of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Convergence Policy Act of the Philippines of 2004.\" This bill defines \"convergence\" as the progressive integration of segments of the information and content industries, including telecommunications, broadcasting, electronic commerce and data processing, into a single economic market based on distributed digital technology. It provides for the management of an orderly transition from the existing arrangements of traditional communications industry structures to a more globalised convergence environment; the development of a national framework that responds to global opportunities and challenges of convergence, and the establishment of transparent and stable regulatory and administrative processes that encourage competition; the delegation of respective powers and functions of the DOTC and the NTC; and the Government's powers to develop specific implementation arrangements as the need arises.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL TOURISM POLICY AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: \"National Tourism Policy Act of 2004.\" This bill states that the national policy for tourism must: 1) guide the course and pace of tourism development and ensure continuity of programs; 2) coordinate the functions and resources of government agencies in tourism programs and enlist the participation of the private sector, local communities and indigenous peoples towards the attainment of such policies; and 3) improve the quality of life of the people by promoting ecotourism as a strategy for low-impact, environmentally sound and community participatory tourism programs that promote a balance between economic development and environment and natural resource protection.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06088

rows.author: A024
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09333) enacted on 2004-09-21
rows.title_full: AN ACT SETTING THE DATE OF THE REGULAR ELECTIONS OF THE REGIONAL GOVERNOR, REGIONAL VICE-GOVERNOR AND MEMBERS OF THE REGIONAL LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY OF THE AUTONOMOUS REGION IN MUSLIM MINDANAO, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.status: Substituted by HB02808

rows.author: A040
rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING HEADS AND CHIEFS OF HOSPITALS TO APPROVE PURCHASE OF MEDICINES AND OTHER MEDICAL SUPPLIES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 344 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS \"THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991\", AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill mandates that in the procurement of medicines and other medical supplies necessary for the delivery of basic health services, the heads of departments and chiefs of hospitals, duly authorized by concerned local chief executives, may approve such disbursements.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2004-08-16

rows.author: A040
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 106 AND 114 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS \"THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991\" AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill strengthens the Local Development Councils (LDCs) by providing for the mandatory inclusion of duly approved local development plans in the plans of higher LDCs and programs and plans of national government agencies for specific local governments.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-08-16

rows.author: A040
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE ROLE OF LOCAL HEALTH OFFICERS IN AREA-BASED HEALTH PLANNING, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 478 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OHTERWISE KNOWN AS \"THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991\", AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill mandates the local health officers to coordinate with the Department of Health (DOH) and other local government units (LGUs) to ensure an integrated approach in the delivery of health care services through area-based health planning. It also requires the local health officers to complement health services being provided by the DOH and the other LGUs through comprehensive health care agreements and other instruments.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-08-16

rows.author: A040
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE LOCAL SCHOOL BOARDS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 98, 99 AND 100 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991\" AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill strengthens the Local School Boards by increasing its membership to include a representative from an accredited nongovernment or people's organization involved in non-formal education and training programs. It further directs the Boards to formulate the school building program, subject to the approval of the concerned sanggunian, and undertake the selection of the site of the schools. It furthermore integrates non-formal education and training programs in the priorities of the annual school board budget.
rows.status: Approved by the Committee on 2005-01-12

rows.author: A040
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE CRITERIA IN THE ACCREDITATION OF NONGOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 108 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS \"THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991\", AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill provides for specific criteria for the accreditation of nongovernmental and people's organizations (NGOs/POs) by requiring them to register with the concerned government agency and have a strong organizational capability as shown by their track record in project development and implementation. It also provides that in the case of pre-qualifications, bids and awards committee, the NGO or PO or any of its officers must have no conflict of interest in the awarding of infrastructure projects and that no local government official or public officer should interfere in the selection process.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-08-16

rows.author: A040
rows.title_full: AN ACT RESTORING THE TAX AND DUTY EXEMPTION PRIVILEGES OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES COMMISSARY AND EXCHANGE SERVICE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill restores the tax and duty exemptions granted to the Armed Forces of the Philippines Commissary and Exchange Services (AFPCES) to better realize its objective of augmenting the wages of Filipino soldiers and ease the economic burden of their widows and orphans, as well as that of the veterans.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2004-08-16

rows.author: A040
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A RECYCLING CENTER IN EVERY BARANGAY NATIONWIDE, APPOPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill establishes a recycling center in every barangay, aimed at: a) promoting and providing for a healthful environment; b) reducing waste generated at sources; c) enhancing the capability of the barangay in environment and solid waste management; and d) providing for income from garbage as a revenue source for barangays.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-08-16

rows.author: A035
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE SAMAR ISLAND SOCIO-ECONOMIC PLANNING AND DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2004-08-16

rows.author: A035
rows.mother_status: Business for the day on 2005-08-03
rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING EXCISE TAX ON CARBONATED DRINKS, FRUIT JUICE DRINKS AND POWDERED JUICE DRINKS AND ON A CERTAIN NON-ESSENTIAL ARTICLES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 150 OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE, AS AMENDED, AND INSERTING A NEW SECTION THEREOF
rows.abstract: This bill imposes, in addition to the 10% value-added tax, a 20% excise tax on selected goods and appliances such as high-priced carpets made of wool or fine animal hair and whirpool bath tubs purchased mostly by those who can well afford to own such goods and appliances. It also imposes a 10% excise tax on carbonated drinks, fruit juice drinks, including those from liquid concentrates and powdered juice drinks.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04241

rows.author: A035
rows.title_full: AN ACT RATIONALIZING AND REGULATING TUITION AND OTHER SCHOOL FEES IN ALL HIGHER AND BASIC EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS, CREATING A TUITION FEE RATIONALIZING COUNCIL AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Tuition Fee Rationalization Act of 2004.\" This bill establishes a tuition fee rationalization council to be headed by a multi-sectoral body that will serve as the highest policy-making body on matters pertaining to tuition fee rates and other increases or adjustments in school fees.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2004-08-16

rows.author: A035
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING A MECHANISM FOR GENERATING QUALITY GRADUATES OF HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS BASED ON PERFORMANCE IN PROFESSIONAL LICENSURE EXAMINATIONS
rows.abstract: \"Professional Examination Zero-Performance Policy Act.\" This bill seeks to permanently revoke government recognition and/or permit to operate pertinent and related professional courses by any higher education institution, whether public or private, whose graduates have registered zero-performance in any professional board or bar examination in three (3) out of five (5) consecutive times they participated in.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2004-08-16

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE AUTOMATIC RELEASE OF THE TEN PERCENT (10%) ALLOCATION TO THE SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN FROM THE GENERAL FUND OF THE BARANGAY AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 329 AND 331 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to free the Sangguniang Kabataan from having to beg to the Barangay Captains for the release of the ten percent (10%) allocation due them.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-08-16

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING RETIREMENT BENEFITS TO ALL BARANGAY OFFICIALS AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 393 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: This bill entitles the barangay officials to retirement benefits from the GSIS after having served for at least nine (9) years of cumulative service, thus giving them due recognition for their dedication and invaluable service.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-08-16

rows.author: E023
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING INSURANCE BENEFITS TO BARANGAY TANODS AND INCREASING THE AMOUNT OF THE COVERAGE OF INSURANCE BENEFITS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6942 AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: This bill increases by at least fifty percent (50%) but not more than one hundred percent (100%), the insurance benefits accorded to all local officials who do not receive fixed salaries during their incumbency as per R.A. 6942.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-08-16

rows.author: D025
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE OPEN LEARNING SYSTEM IN THE PHILIPPINES APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Open Learning System Act of 2004.\" This bill seeks to utilize the distance teaching/learning system where students shall not be required to regularly attend conventional classrooms, thus allowing these students to study while working in offices, factories, farms or other preoccupations.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2004-08-16

rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE USE OF THE CONTRACTOR'S CERTIFICATE AS A LEGAL PAPER THAT CAN BE USED AS COLLATERAL AND REDISCOUNTING IN ANY WINDOW OF A PUBLIC OR PRIVATE BANK
rows.abstract: To protect the credit standing of the contractor and the agency, the bill proposes the acceptance of the contractor's certificate as a collateral to secure loans and be rediscounted at any bank.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2004-08-16

rows.author: A061
rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE ISSUANCE OF LEGAL INSTRUMENT TO COVER THE FUNDS FOR THE CHARATER LOANS TO THE GOVERNMENT AND PRIVATE WORKERS
rows.abstract: This bill authorizes the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) and the Social Security System to grant loans in the amount of One Hundred Thousand Pesos (P100,000.00) to government and private employees who have rendered fifteen (15) to twenty (20) years of continuous service.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2004-08-16

rows.author: A061
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE SALARIES OF THE DAY CARE TEACHERS/WORKERS WITH CORRESPONDING BENEFITS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: This bill provides for the inclusion in the regular General Appropriations Act an amount intended for the salaries and benefits of the Day Care Teachers and the Day Care Workers nationwide. The sum necessary for implementation of this Act shall be charged against the annual budget of the Department of Social Welfare and Development.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SOCIAL SERVICES since 2004-08-16

rows.author: A061
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A FIVE (5) YEAR MORATORIUM IN THE IMPOSITION OF NEW TAXES IN ALL PRODUCTS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill hopes to relieve poor consumers from paying and buying highly taxed products for at least five (5) years.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2004-08-16

rows.author: D090
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09346) enacted on 2006-06-24
rows.title_full: AN ACT ABOLISHING THE DEATH PENALTY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill states that the death penalty law symbolizes the retributive justice that is adopted by the penal system and violates the Constitutional provision of cruel and excessive punishment. It further states that there is no clear indication, so far, that its imposition has deterred the continued commission of heinous crimes.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04826

rows.author: D053
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING ONE STEP SALARY GRADE INCREASE TO GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES ONE YEAR BEFORE COMPULSORY RETIREMENT AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: This bill hopes that government employees will be assured of an increase in their lump sum retirement benefits and monthly pensions to enable them to be better-off economically, and be able to respond to their needs and their family's as well.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2004-08-16

rows.author: D053
rows.title_full: AN ACT UPGRADING THE MINIMUM SALARY GRADE LEVEL OF PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS IN ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY LEVELS FROM GRADE 10 TO GRADE 17 AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: This bill aims to entice competent and highly qualified educators to join the public teaching force and recognizes the critical social responsibility that they shoulder by upgrading their minimum salary levels from Grade 10 to Grade 17.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-08-16

rows.author: D053
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1949 ENTITLED 'ESTABLISHING A JUDICIARY DEVELOPMENT FUND' AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill democratizes the use of the Judiciary Development Fund by providing that at least ninety percent (90%) of the Fund shall be used for cost of living allowances, and not more than ten percent (10%) shall be used for office equipment and facilities in the Courts where the legal fees are collected.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-08-16

rows.author: D053
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING ALL FORMS OF SMUGGLING AS ECONOMIC SABOTAGE AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREOF
rows.abstract: This bill declares it a State policy to control all forms of actual and technical smuggling that impinge upon the genuine attainment of economic growth and development.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2004-08-16

rows.author: D053
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE RATIONALIZATION OF SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND BENEFITS OF OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES OF GOVERNMENT OWNED OR CONTROLLED CORPORATIONS AND GOVERNMENT FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS EXEMPTED FROM THE COMPENSATION AND POSITION CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM
rows.abstract: This bill proposes the exemption of all officials and employees of government owned or controlled corporations and government financial institutions from the Compensation and Position Classification System provided that their compensation shall be no more than twice the salaries of equivalent ranks and positions in other government agencies.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-08-16

rows.author: D053
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09340) enacted on 2005-09-22
rows.title_full: AN ACT POSTPONING THE 2005 BARANGAY AND SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN ELECTIONS AND HOLDING THE SAME IN MAY 2007 TO COINCIDE WITH THE LOCAL ELECTIONS
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to synchronized the barangay elections with the local elections on May 2007 in order to save the government from additional expenses and effort.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03742

rows.author: D053
rows.title_full: AN ACT REDEFINING THE COMPOSITION OF BARANGAY OFFICIALS AND INCREASING THE BENEFITS OF BARANGAY OFFICIALS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 387 AND 393 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: This bill provides for the appointment of a barangay social worker and a barangay health worker in every municipality. It increases the honoraria allowances and other emoluments of the barangay officials, including barangay social workers, barangay health workers and barangay tanods.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-08-16

rows.author: E045
rows.mother_status: Senate requested for a conference committee on 2007-02-08
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO EXTEND THE UTILIZATION PERIOD OF THE AGRICULTURAL COMPETITIVENESS ENHANCEMENT FUND, AMENDING SECTION 8 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8178, ENTITLED 'AN ACT REPLACING QUANTITATIVE IMPORT RESTRICTION ON AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS, EXCEPT RICE, WITH TARIFFS, CREATING THE AGRICULTURAL COMPETITIVENESS ENHANCEMENT FUND, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill extends the utilization period of the Agricultural Competitiveness Ehancement Fund (ACEF) by 10 years to enable the governent to provide the farming sector the opportunity to use said funds to strengthen their development activities and enhance their competitiveness.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03740
